NVIDIA's Blackwell generation has been positioned as
a uniform advance over Hopper, and the B300 (Blackwell
Ultra) as an advance over the B200: 288 GB of HBM3e
against 192 GB, and roughly 8 TB/s of memory bandwidth.
Research computing centers must convert such specifications
into procurement decisions, yet application-level speedup is
governed by memory access patterns, launch overhead, col-
lective communication, and above all by the maturity of the
vendor software stack at the moment of purchase.

ter's representative workloads on both parts. Our contributions

ference and DDP training, LLM inference at two model
scales and three precisions, a 3D vision transformer, and
six HPC codes (Section IV, Section V).
•A

Throughput alone cannot separate a device that is working
hard and losing from one that is idle. Board power can. Table I

VI. DISCUSSION ANDRECOMMENDATIONS
Two conclusions follow that a specification sheet would not
have predicted.
First, the B300 should be purchased for what it is: a part
optimized for large-GEMM, low-precision transformer work
with a large weight footprint. It is the better choice for ViT-
class inference and training, where it wins on both throughput
and energy efficiency, and for workloads gated on per-device
capacity. It is the worse choice for convolutional networks, for
FP64 codes, and — at present — for 70B LLM serving.

evaluation_independence.corroboration_summary: Cross-cluster replication on two independently administered systems and the monotonic alignment between measured power saturation and throughput deficits corroborate the central diagnostic claims.
evaluation_independence.final_evaluation_signal: Headline outcomes are established by objective physical and execution measurements: NVML board power draw, throughput in FPS/tokens/s/ns/day, latency, and wall time, with no learned or automated evaluator producing the reported results.
evaluation_independence.optimization_signal: The systems under study are not trained or tuned by the authors; the relevant shaping signals are vendor software-stack choices, including cuDNN heuristic kernel selection with autotuning disabled and the specific vLLM builds used on each cluster.

primary.claim_evidence_alignment: Claims that B300 is not a universal upgrade over B200 and suffers on small-kernel or FP64 workloads are directly substantiated by measured throughput deficits and power saturation metrics. The authors clearly distinguish conclusively proven hardware behavior from software-stack effects.
primary.evaluation_assessment: The evaluation spans multiple standard AI models and production HPC applications, reporting throughput, latency, and power metrics. The authors rigorously report run replications, noting medians across five runs for HPC and 3D ViT benchmarks and documenting 2-4% run-to-run variation bounds for single-run CV and LLM sweeps.

evaluation_independence.corroboration_summary: Cross-cluster replication across two independent administrative environments and alignment between physical power saturation data and runtime performance corroborate the headline findings.
evaluation_independence.final_evaluation_signal: Objective execution metrics consisting of measured throughput (FPS, tokens/s, ns/day) and physical board power draw sampled via NVML.
evaluation_independence.optimization_signal: Standard vendor-recommended configurations and library heuristics (e.g., cuDNN heuristic kernel selection and default vLLM configurations).

primary.limitations: The authors clearly delineate limitations, including the lack of B300 allocations for certain single-GPU molecular dynamics benchmarks, single-run iterations for some AI sweeps, toolchain version differences across hardware generations, and the exclusion of host-side input data pipeline effects.
primary.method_assessment: The methodology is thoroughly detailed, describing execution harnesses that isolate GPU kernel execution from host transfer bottlenecks, sampling board power via NVML at 20 Hz, and tracking exact software stacks (CUDA, PyTorch, cuDNN, and vLLM). Comparisons across two separate hardware vendor nodes directly test software maturity and build artifacts.
primary.quality_rationale: The study offers a well-scoped, rigorously controlled systems evaluation with reproducible artifacts and nuanced empirical explanations, meeting high scientific standards for empirical benchmarking.
primary.scoped_contribution: The manuscript presents an empirical, power-resolved benchmark comparing NVIDIA B200 and B300 GPUs across computer vision, LLM inference, 3D vision transformers, and scientific HPC workloads on two independent clusters, identifying workload-dependent regressions and software build impacts.
